variants.headline: Looking back: party leader faces a public scandal
variants.sub: A party leader is the subject of a newly revealed scandal.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A scandal concerning a party leader had come to light in {colony}.

Our political principles ought to survive the discomfort of applying them to leaders. Trust is not a private asset belonging to a party hierarchy. It concerns the people asked to give their support, and they deserve an argument about responsibility that does not depend on convenient invention.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

This paper treats {target} as a subject for scrutiny, while withholding conclusions the reported revelation does not establish. Attention to trust need not depend upon an invented account of wrongdoing.

variants.headline: Looking back: leadership under an unwelcome spotlight
variants.sub: A scandal about a party leader has become public in the colony.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: A party leader was the subject of a newly revealed scandal.

Our political principles ought to survive the discomfort of applying them to leaders. Trust is not a private asset belonging to a party hierarchy. It concerns the people asked to give their support, and they deserve an argument about responsibility that does not depend on convenient invention.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

This paper treats {target} as a subject for scrutiny, while withholding conclusions the reported revelation does not establish. Attention to trust need not depend upon an invented account of wrongdoing.

variants.headline: Looking back: a scandal tests political trust
variants.sub: A scandal concerning a party leader has come to light in {colony}.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: A scandal about a party leader had become public in the colony.

Our political principles ought to survive the discomfort of applying them to leaders. Trust is not a private asset belonging to a party hierarchy. It concerns the people asked to give their support, and they deserve an argument about responsibility that does not depend on convenient invention.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.
